Investing.com — Intel (NASDAQ: INTC) shares plunged 20% Thursday after the chipmaker forecast fourth-quarter earnings and revenue well below Wall Street expectations, overshadowing a stronger-than-expected third-quarter profit and surging demand for data-center processors.

Still guessing which stocks will beat the market? Our AI portfolio updates monthly and is outperforming the S&P 500 by 118%. See this month's list »

Intel reported third-quarter adjusted earnings of $0.52 per share, beating analyst estimates of $0.40. Revenue rose 21% year over year to $16.5 billion, slightly above consensus of $16.48 billion.

The outlook was considerably weaker. Intel forecast fourth-quarter revenue of $15 billion to $16 billion, below analyst expectations of $17.08 billion. At the midpoint, the range implies a shortfall of about 9%. Adjusted earnings are expected to reach $0.25 per share, compared with consensus of $0.44.

The guidance comes as Intel faces contrasting trends across its businesses, with strong demand for server CPUs helping offset weakness in the PC market.

"Despite near-term headwinds across the PC industry, demand for our CPUs remains robust," Chief Executive Lip-Bu Tan said, adding that the results reflected improving execution, expanded supply and progress in process technology.

Chief Financial Officer David Zinsner said Intel expects PC market weakness to continue through at least the first half of next year.

Revenue from Intel's Client Computing and Physical AI Group fell 5% year over year to $8.1 billion in the third quarter, reflecting the industry slowdown. By contrast, revenue from its Data Center and AI segment surged 78% to $7.3 billion, marking the strongest data-center revenue growth in 15 years, according to Zinsner.

Intel's profitability outlook also disappointed. Adjusted gross margin expanded to 44.1% in the third quarter from 40% a year earlier, but the company expects the metric to decline to 38% in the fourth quarter.

Intel Foundry revenue increased 58% year over year to $6.7 billion. The company generated $5.1 billion in operating cash flow during the quarter, while investors continue to assess whether its manufacturing business can attract enough external customers to support its long-term investment plans.

Updates on foundry customer commitments, manufacturing capacity and Intel's next-generation process roadmap could provide further clues about the company's turnaround when management discusses the results on its earnings call.

Intel Corp (NASDAQ:INTC, XETRA:INL) shares plunged 16% on Thursday evening after the chipmaker issued a weaker-than-expected fourth-quarter outlook, overshadowing stronger-than-forecast earnings and robust growth in its data center business.

Third-quarter revenue rose 21% year over year to $16.5 billion, in line with analyst estimates, while adjusted earnings per share of $0.52 beat expectations of $0.40.

Non-GAAP gross margin reached 44.1%, above the 42.1% consensus estimate and up 4.1 percentage points year over year.

However, Intel's fourth-quarter guidance fell short of expectations across revenue, earnings and margins. The company forecast revenue of $15 billion to $16 billion, below the $17.1 billion analysts had expected.

Adjusted earnings per share are projected at $0.25, compared with estimates of $0.43, while non-GAAP gross margin is expected to reach 38%, against consensus of 42.4%.

Management warned that weakness in the personal computer market would persist into next year.

"Looking ahead, we see the PC slowdown continuing at least through the first half of next year," Intel CFO David Zinsner said, while expressing optimism about opportunities across its broader portfolio.

Intel added that it would continue making disciplined investments in capacity and working capital to increase supply and support future growth.

The third-quarter results showed stronger demand in data center operations. Revenue from Intel's Data Center and AI division climbed 78% year over year to $7.3 billion, beating analyst estimates of $6.46 billion. Intel described the performance as its strongest data center revenue growth in 15 years.

The Client Computing Group, which includes PC-related products, reported revenue of $8.1 billion, down 5% year over year. Intel Foundry revenue increased 58% to $6.7 billion, while total Intel Products revenue rose 22% to $15.4 billion.

Operating cash flow reached $5.1 billion, ahead of the $4.9 billion estimate, while adjusted free cash flow was $1.6 billion. Gross capital expenditure fell 43% year over year to $4.2 billion.

Intel also completed a $23 billion public equity offering and released version 0.9 of its Intel 14A process design kit in October.

The results point to progress in data center demand and profitability, but the weaker outlook highlights the near-term challenges facing Intel as PC market softness weighs on its recovery.

Intel (INTC) Q3 2026 highlights:

Revenue $16.51 billion vs S&P analysts' consensus estimates of $16.42 billion (20.9% year-on-year growth, 0.6% beat)

Adjusted EPS $0.52 vs S&P analysts' consensus estimates of $0.40 (30.6% beat)

Operating margin 15.3%, up from 5% in the same quarter last year

Free cash flow margin 9.9%, up from 0.9% in the same quarter last year

Inventory days outstanding 126, up from 118 in the previous quarter

Market capitalization $502 billion

"Our Q3 results demonstrate improving execution, meaningful progress expanding supply and continued advancement of our process technology," said Lip-Bu Tan, Intel CEO. "Despite near-term headwinds across the PC industry, demand for our CPUs remains robust, reinforcing our confidence in the long-term growth opportunities for our business. Our immediate priority is to unlock additional supply to meet extraordinary demand for our Xeon family, while strengthening our product portfolio and roadmap. We are moving with urgency and focus to capitalize on these opportunities to deliver sustainable growth and long-term shareholder value."

Revenue growth

Reviewing a company's long-term revenue performance reveals insights into its quality. Any business can have short-term success, but a top-tier one grows for years. Intel's demand was weak over the last five years as its revenue fell at a 5% annual rate. That outcome points to poor business quality. Semiconductors are a cyclical industry, and long-term investors should be prepared for periods of high growth followed by periods of revenue contractions.

Long-term growth is the most important, but short-term results matter for semiconductors because the rapid pace of technological innovation (Moore's Law) could make yesterday's hit product obsolete today. Intel's annualized revenue growth of 5.1% over the last two years is above its five-year trend, which is encouraging.

Intel (INTC) is back in focus after a 5.2% jump that followed fresh commentary on tight memory chip supply and heavy semiconductor equipment spending, set against a backdrop of rising AI-related demand.

For context, Intel's share price has pulled back over the past month, with a 30 day share price return of down 17.7%. However, the broader trend remains strong, with a year to date share price return of 142.6% and a 1 year total shareholder return of 131.1%, as investors weigh a heavy AI and foundry investment cycle against fresh deals in cloud, enterprise AI and quantum computing.

Scan beyond Intel and focus on AI infrastructure opportunities with our curated list of 54 AI infrastructure stocks.

Intel's sharp rebound sits between two stories. Either the surge tracks real progress in AI, foundry, and quantum bets, or sentiment has simply snapped back after a steep pullback. It is time to test that against the current valuation.

Most Popular Narrative: 81% Undervalued

Intel's most followed narrative pegs fair value at $500.93 against a last close of $95.53, a large gap that suggests the recent AI and foundry optimism is only partly reflected in the share price.

Reasons I bought Intel:

• x86 software. A lot of existing software has been created for the x86 architecture and additionally has likely been optimized to run on Intel CPUs due to them having been the consistent market leader for so long, giving them an advantage over AMD.

• This is most noticed when comparing applications using IBOT or Intel Compiler.

See why 91 investors see Intel as 81% undervalued.

According to Suen, the narrative leans heavily on Intel's established x86 software base and foundry footprint, then discounts those future cash flows at 11.31% to arrive at an intrinsic value that is much higher than the current share price.

The fair value estimate of $500.93 is therefore not just a price target; it is the end point of a cash flow stream that assumes Intel's AI, data center, and US based foundry assets continue to attract workloads and customers over time.

Result: Fair Value of $500.93 (UNDERVALUED)

However, Intel's story can break if x86 software loyalty weakens, or if US based foundry economics disappoint compared with lower cost and geopolitically exposed Asian rivals.

Another View: Intel Through the SWS DCF Lens

The popular Intel narrative points to an 81% discount to fair value, yet the SWS DCF model paints a different picture. On this approach, Intel's last close of $95.53 sits above an estimated future cash flow value of $88.43, which implies the stock screens as overvalued on this method.

SANTA CLARA, Calif. (AP) — SANTA CLARA, Calif. (AP) — Intel Corp. (INTC) on Thursday reported third-quarter profit of $3.32 billion.

The Santa Clara, California-based company said it had profit of 60 cents per share. Earnings, adjusted for one-time gains and costs, came to 52 cents per share.

The results beat Wall Street expectations. The average estimate of 14 analysts surveyed by Zacks Investment Research was for earnings of 39 cents per share.

The world's largest chipmaker posted revenue of $16.51 billion in the period, also beating Street forecasts. Thirteen analysts surveyed by Zacks expected $16.44 billion.

For the current quarter ending in December, Intel expects its per-share earnings to be 25 cents.

The company said it expects revenue in the range of $15 billion to $16 billion for the fiscal fourth quarter.
